instructions:
You are an embodied agent exploring an unknown synthetic indoor room and reconstructing an object map. Think carefully. You can use native Codex shell commands, view_image, file edits, and persistent files in /work to plan, compute, and remember. Use view_image on images to actually see them. Do not infer unseen furniture from priors. Do not merge distinct identical objects or duplicate repeated observations. No ground truth or evaluator feedback is accessible.
Public environment API: python3 /app/act.py '{"turn_deg": 30, "move_m": 0.5}' rotates clockwise then moves along the new heading, and returns ONE new RGB path and execution status. turn_deg in [-90,90], move_m in [-0.75,0.75]. Negative movement moves backward. Zero/zero observes. Use a fresh action_id only for a new action; the script assigns one by default. A partial/blocked action may move less than requested. RGB resolution 512x512, horizontal/vertical FOV 90 degrees, camera height 1.55 m. The initial view direction defines +y of your map; initial camera right defines +x. Start is (0,0), units meters. No measured pose or depth is provided. Scene geometry is fixed. Each call acquires one frame including repeated views. Total budget is 200 frames. You may stop early if sufficient evidence; explicitly write stop_reason="early_stop".
The same exploration is read out at 20,40,60,80,100,120,150,200 frames. Movement pauses at a checkpoint. Keep persistent notes as needed and resume exploration in the next segment. Only the last eight image occurrences are retained in the model context; older images remain available in /work/observations for selective re-reading, and all action receipts in /work/history.jsonl. Your text and notes remain. This is an explicit recent-image harness.
At the checkpoint write /work/map.json with {"frame":"start_camera_xy","units":"meters","objects":[{"id":"your_stable_instance_id","category":"plain generic category","x":number_or_null,"y":number_or_null,"confidence":0_to_1,"evidence":[{"frame_id":"obs_0001","pixel_xy":[x,y]}]}],"stop_reason":"checkpoint"}. x/y are object ground-center positions relative to START, not camera coordinates. Include uncertain objects with null position rather than inventing a location. The evidence field is optional. Then finish the response. Use shell commands to write JSON files. Do not write a fake map before viewing images. Do not read unrelated files or attempt to access any hidden scene source.

<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of instructions provided through a `SKILL.md` source. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and source locator. `file` locators are on the host filesystem, `environment resource` locators are owned by an execution environment, `orchestrator resource` locators are opaque non-filesystem resources, and `custom resource` locators use their provider's access mechanism.
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: /work/.codex/skills/.system/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: /work/.codex/skills/.system/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: /work/.codex/skills/.system/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations. (file: /work/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: /work/.codex/skills/.system/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

<permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions>

Continue the mapping task until checkpoint 20 (total exploration budget remains 200 frames). Controller count: 0 frames acquired; 20 more frames remain until this checkpoint. Start by acquiring and viewing the first RGB. When the checkpoint is reached, write /work/map.json and finish this segment. You may explicitly choose early_stop.

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Runs a command in a PTY, returning output or a session ID for ongoing interaction.

justification.description: User-facing approval question for `require_escalated`; omit otherwise.

login.description: True runs the shell with -l/-i semantics; false disables them. Defaults to true.

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

prefix_rule.description: Reusable approval prefix for `cmd`, only with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`; for example ["git", "pull"].

sandbox_permissions.description: Per-command sandbox override. Defaults to `use_default`; use `require_escalated` for unsandboxed execution.

shell.description: Shell binary to launch. Defaults to the user's default shell.

tty.description: True allocates a PTY for the command; false or omitted uses plain pipes.

workdir.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the turn cwd.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Defaults to 10000 ms; effective range is 250-30000 ms.

tools.name: write_stdin
tools.description: Writes characters to an existing unified exec session and returns recent output.

chars.description: Bytes to write to stdin. Defaults to empty, which polls without writing.

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

session_id.description: Identifier of the running unified exec session.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Non-empty writes default to 250 ms and cap at 30000 ms; empty polls wait 5000-300000 ms by default.

Updates the task plan.
Provide an optional explanation and a list of plan items, each with a step and status.
At most one step can be in_progress at a time.

explanation.description: Optional explanation for this plan update.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

format.definition:
start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change_move: "*** Move to: " filename LF
change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

%import common.LF

tools.description: View a local image file from the filesystem when visual inspection is needed. Use this for images already available on disk.

detail.description: Image detail level. Defaults to `high`; use `original` to preserve exact resolution.

path.description: Local filesystem path to an image file.

tools.description:
# Tool discovery

Searches over deferred tool metadata with BM25 and exposes matching tools for the next model call.

You have access to tools from the following sources:
- Multi-agent tools: Spawn and manage sub-agents.
Some of the tools may not have been provided to you upfront, and you should use this tool (`tool_search`) to search for the required tools. For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search` instead of `list_mcp_resources` or `list_mcp_resource_templates`.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Defaults to 8.
